chunks: Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār, from Ṣafwān, from Ḥamzah ibn Ḥumrān, from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “The likeness of salat (prayer) is the likeness of the central pole of a tent: when the pole is firmly set, the ropes, pegs, and covering are beneficial; but when it breaks, no rope, peg, or covering is of any benefit.”

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the central act of worship being emphasized
key_terms.الْأَطْنَابُ: tent ropes, representing supporting elements connected to the main pillar
key_terms.الْأَوْتَادُ: tent pegs, further supporting parts that only function with the central pole intact
key_terms.الْغِشَاءُ: covering of the tent, the outer structure that depends on the pillar
key_terms.الْفُسْطَاطِ: tent, the image used to illustrate the structure of religious life
key_terms.انْكَسَرَ: broke, indicating collapse of the essential support
key_terms.عَمُودِ: pillar or central support, used as a metaphor for what upholds everything else

ai.seo_question: Why is salat (prayer) described as the foundation of a believer’s religious life?
ai.summary: This hadith presents salat (prayer) as the central support of religious life, like the main pole that upholds a tent. It teaches that other acts depend on the soundness of salat, highlighting its foundational importance and central place in worship.
